paragraphs.source_en: The battlefront had been stretched needlessly long. Everything west of Mikawa ought to have been securely in their grasp, yet enemy remnants still dotted many places. At Otsu in Omi, not far from the capital, Kyogoku Takatsugu still stubbornly refused to submit. At Tanabe in Tango, Yusai, the father of Hosokawa Tadaoki, was likewise holding the castle with dogged resolve. Fukushima Masanori, stationed at Kiyosu in Owari, appeared to have gone over completely to Ieyasu. Maeda Toshinaga, who should have stood beside Mitsunari, had turned his forces around and was poised to strike the domain of Otani Gyobu.

paragraphs.source_en: There had been one success: he had won over Oda Hidenobu of Gifu. Yet if Fukushima Masanori welcomed Ieyasu into Kiyosu and then attacked Hidenobu, there would be fresh cause for anxiety. Hidenobu was Nobunaga's legitimate grandson—the Sanboshi whom Hideyoshi had once designated heir to the Oda house. Mitsunari had sent his retainer Kawase Samanosuke to Hidenobu, and only after exhausting every argument and device had he finally brought him into the fold.

paragraphs.source_en: Then there was the further difficulty of choosing someone to command the war. Ukita Hideie might be one of the Five Elders, but he lacked authority.
